en: And so you get grounded in knowledge of what's happening and you get to use that data to figure out how to make decisions in addition to all the notes you have and deal memos you've written perhaps over the years or insights you've had about like how to choose founders.
zh: 于是你能立足于对行业动态的了解，并利用这些数据来决策，再结合你多年来积累的所有笔记、可能写过的投资备忘录，或者关于如何挑选创始人的洞察。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're essentially composing insights from your personal lived experience, your notes, public data to make decisions.
zh: 你本质上是在组合来自你亲身经历的洞察、你的笔记、公开数据来做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, you pay PitchBook by the seat, but now you're running a bunch of agents, and your agents can perhaps not access everything you can on PitchBook, or you're doing like sort of this to get a browser, perhaps against terms of service to send an agent via browser to PitchBook using your auth credentials, and it's inefficient, it's clunky, right?
zh: 现在，你按席位付费用 PitchBook,但现在你在运行大量智能体，而你的智能体可能无法访问你在 PitchBook 上能访问的一切，或者你在做类似这种操作：用一个浏览器——可能违反服务条款——用你的认证凭据通过浏览器把一个智能体发到 PitchBook 上，这很低效、很笨拙，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But clearly their data is valuable, and clearly your agent should have convenient access to it.
zh: 但显然他们的数据是有价值的，显然你的智能体应该能方便地访问它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we figure out how valuable pitch book data is for your agents to make your decisions, because clearly you're investing a large hundreds of millions of dollars.
zh: 所以如果我们能搞清楚 PitchBook 的数据对你的智能体做决策有多大价值——因为你显然在投资数亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So clearly you presume that you make a great return on that.
zh: 那么显然你假定自己能从中获得很好的回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this data is truly valuable if you depend on it today.
zh: 所以如果你今天依赖这些数据，那它就是真正有价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you should be able to figure out how to compensate pitch book for the data, even when agents use it, which is not by the seat.
zh: 所以你应该能想出如何为此向 PitchBook 支付报酬，即使是在智能体使用数据时——而不是按席位计费。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we figure that out, it will be a huge market and agents will be better off.
zh: 如果我们想清楚这一点，这将是一个巨大的市场，智能体也会过得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we don't figure it out, you're going to be in this weird cat and mouse game of PitchBook being like, no, I want to sell you a seat.
zh: 如果我们想不清楚，你就会陷入这种奇怪的猫鼠游戏:PitchBook 说，不行，我要卖给你的是席位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to shut it off.
zh: 我要把你关掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your agent is stuck without the data.
zh: 于是你的智能体就没有数据可用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you're involved in pulling data.
zh: 然后你就开始费劲去抓取数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every big company has the choice today of do we let agents in or do we keep them out?
zh: 我认为今天每一家大公司都面临选择：我们是让智能体进来，还是把它们挡在外面？

speaker: Unknown
en: And Amazon has said, I'm sorry, in most recent times, Muse, you will not be let into our garden.
zh: 而 Amazon 最近说了，很抱歉，Muse,你不会被放进我们的花园。

speaker: Unknown
en: Shopify has said, come in, baby.
zh: Shopify 说，进来吧，宝贝。

speaker: Unknown
en: Expedia has said, come in.
zh: Expedia 说，进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does this play out?
zh: 这会如何演变？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think eventually everyone has to let them in.
zh: 我认为最终所有人都得放它们进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is on what terms?
zh: 问题是按什么条件？

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you align incentives for everyone?
zh: 那么你如何为所有人调整激励机制？

speaker: Unknown
en: And people are going to have to play their strategy games on how they win in this new world.
zh: 而人们将不得不玩他们的策略游戏，看如何在这个新世界里取胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Literally the customer is changing in front of our eyes, right?
zh: 说真的，客户正在我们眼前发生变化，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the customer used to be a human.
zh: 以前客户是人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're building products for humans.
zh: 你在为人类构建产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you're building products for agents or you're building agents.
zh: 现在你在为智能体构建产品，或者你在构建智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now you have to figure out what your place in this new reality will be.
zh: 所以现在你必须想清楚，在这个新现实中你将处于什么位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't know if there's a right or wrong answer here.
zh: 而我不知道这里是否有对或错的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also depends on sort of how much market power you have.
zh: 这也在某种程度上取决于你有多少市场支配力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think Amazon were right to say no to Muse?
zh: 你认为 Amazon 拒绝 Muse 是对的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Depends on what they do next with it.
zh: 取决于他们接下来用它做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it turns out that they have sufficient market power to have Muse or other agents connect to them differently, perhaps.
zh: 如果结果证明他们有足够的市场支配力让 Muse 或其他智能体以不同的方式接入他们,或许是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over time, or ship their own agent and drive crazy adoption, let's say they have that capability, then I guess they were right, right?
zh: 随着时间推移,或者推出他们自己的智能体并疯狂推动采用,假设他们有那种能力,那我猜他们是对的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: On the other hand, once they've made this with Nodgla now, anyone else's agent, and they can not ship an agent that consumers use, and they won't allow anyone else's agent to use them,
zh: 另一方面,一旦他们与 Nodgla 做了这个,任何其他人的智能体,而他们可以不推出消费者使用的智能体,并且不允许任何其他人的智能体使用他们,

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the transaction economy starts moving off of two agents, which are all big ifs, by the way, then it would be a bad move.
zh: 而且大量交易经济开始转移到两个智能体上——顺便说一句,这些都是很大的如果——那这将是一个糟糕的举动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I'm betting on agents.
zh: 现在,我押注在智能体上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have mixed feelings around agents and what fraction of e-commerce transactions they do.
zh: 我对智能体以及它们占电商交易的比例有着复杂的感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's unclear, right?
zh: 比如这还不清楚,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's... Do you think it's unclear?
zh: 比如……你认为这不清楚吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's unwaveringly clear.
zh: 我认为这是毫无疑问地清楚的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I'm super early on the adoption curve and I buy everything through instinct now.
zh: 也许我在采用曲线上超级靠前,我现在通过 instinct 购买所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other than holidays and a home, I'm literally just everything's their instinct.
zh: 除了度假和房子,我真的所有东西都是通过 instinct 买的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So me too.
zh: 我也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I also know a lot of people who like to buy things themselves.
zh: 但我也认识很多喜欢自己买东西的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, listen, we want to delegate to agents things which we see as chores and uninteresting and not delegate to agents things that give us joy or pleasure or make us have fun doing those things.
zh: 而且,听着,我们想把那些我们视为苦差事和无聊的事情委托给智能体,而不把那些给我们带来快乐、愉悦或让我们做起来觉得有趣的事情委托给智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know people who don't want to delegate shopping.
zh: 而且我认识那些不想把购物委托出去的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want to delegate a lot of things in their life.
zh: 他们想把生活中很多东西委托出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't want to delegate shopping.
zh: 他们不想把购物委托出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why I don't know the distribution of these people and how behavior changes, but it might be people give away a lot of other chores and then spend a lot of time shopping.
zh: 所以这就是为什么我不知道这些人的分布以及行为会如何变化,但可能是人们把很多其他苦差事交出去,然后花大量时间购物。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that does worry me is actually the dissolution of the advertising industry in the wake of agents.
zh: 有一件真正让我担心的事,实际上是智能体兴起后广告业的消解。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I have, you know, if I order my Deliveroo and my Uber, DoorDash for our dear American counterparts,
zh: 如果我,你知道,如果我点我的 Deliveroo 和我的 Uber,以及给我们亲爱的美国同行们的 DoorDash,

speaker: Unknown
en: Through instinct, that Uber banner that's now advertising something becomes worthless.
zh: 通过 instinct,那么 Uber 上现在展示某样东西广告的横幅就变得毫无价值了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazon, their advertising business is bigger than their e-com business now.
zh: Amazon,他们的广告业务现在比他们的电商业务还大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course they're shutting it off because if agents are the primary customer, your ads business goes to next to nothing, correct?
zh: 他们当然要把它关掉,因为如果智能体是主要客户,你的广告业务就几乎归零了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is not just you're talking about this in the e-commerce land, right?
zh: 而且这不只是你在电商领域谈论的这个,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is what I meant early on when I said like the business models have to change.
zh: 但这就是我早些时候说的,商业模式必须改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ads don't work with agents in their current form.
zh: 广告以目前的形式无法与智能体兼容。

speaker: Unknown
en: Forgetting e-commerce for a second, if you think of you're in the content business, let's say your page, which is ad supported, public information on the web, ad supported page, people show up, you show them ads, you make money, great content.
zh: 先把电商放一边,假设你在内容行业,比如你的页面是广告支持的,网络上的公开信息,广告支持的页面,人们来了,你给他们展示广告,你赚钱,很棒的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents show up, no one sees ads, you make no money, which is why we like to pay people
zh: 智能体来了,没有人看到广告,你赚不到钱,这就是为什么我们喜欢付钱给人们

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're effectively building an ad sense for agents showing up to read your content.
zh: 所以我们实际上是在为智能体构建一个广告联盟(AdSense),让它们来读取你的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we like to pay content owners a variable amount of money every time an agent derives benefit from reading their information, which is a variable amount of money is what a visitor to your website will pay you based on a click probability or a value probability on ads.
zh: 所以我们喜欢在每次智能体从阅读他们的信息中获得收益时,向内容所有者支付一笔可变金额的钱,而这笔可变金额的钱,就像你网站访客基于点击概率或价值概率在广告上会付给你的钱一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you do that?
zh: 你们为什么要这么做?

speaker: Unknown
en: To incentive a line content owners.
zh: 为了激励一致地对待内容所有者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, what's going to happen?
zh: 否则,会发生什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's going to block agents.
zh: 所有人都会屏蔽智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need to find a replacement to the ads business model.
zh: 所以你需要找到广告商业模式的替代品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get you, but you have to assume that you're going to be like 100% of the market then, because if you're 30, 40% of the market and you're like, oh, don't worry, we'll pay you.
zh: 我明白你的意思,但你必须假设你将占据市场的 100%,因为如果你只占市场的 30%、40%,然后你说,哦,别担心,我们会付你钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And New York Times is still like, well, thanks, Parag, but 60% of my traffic is still unpaid.
zh: 而 New York Times 还是会说,好吧,谢谢,Parag,但我 60% 的流量仍然是没有报酬的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm just going to block all of you.
zh: 所以我干脆把你们全部屏蔽掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, but I think they're going to block them and not me.
zh: 不,但我认为他们会屏蔽他们,而不是屏蔽我。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to give me a data feed.
zh: 他们会给我一个数据源。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does incentive alignment mean?
zh: 激励一致是什么意思?

speaker: Unknown
en: It means the New York Times believes that I pay them competitive market price or the right price or an attractive price or a fair price.
zh: 它意味着 New York Times 相信我支付给他们有竞争力的市场价格,或合适的价格,或有吸引力的价格,或公平的价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I do that, they should give me their content.
zh: 如果我这么做,他们应该把内容给我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if somebody else doesn't give them that, and if they have the technical levers or legal levers, they shouldn't give it to them.
zh: 而如果别人不给他们那样的条件,而他们有技术杠杆或法律杠杆,他们就不应该把内容给那些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Business is a little bit like music with streaming, which is like the business just becomes candidly much worse for the creators.
zh: 这个业务有点像流媒体时代的音乐行业,坦率地说,这个业务对创作者来说变得糟糕得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it still provides some money and significant money, but they have to get a little bit more creative with alternative streams, touring, merchandise, alternative business.
zh: 而且它仍然提供一些钱和可观的钱,但他们必须在替代收入来源上更有创意一点,比如巡演、周边商品、替代性业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it the same where your core goes down and you have to get more creative?
zh: 是不是也一样，你的核心业务下滑了，你就得更有创造力？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, but I don't think so.
zh: 我不知道，但我不这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's one fundamental thing that is different here.
zh: 我认为这里有一个根本性的不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents using the web 1000x more, like that 1000x, is really different.
zh: 智能体对网络的使用多了一千倍，这一千倍，真的非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, all of a sudden, the amount of utility added goes up if these agents are presumed to be doing something useful.
zh: 现在，突然之间，如果假设这些智能体在做一些有用的事情，那么所增加的效用就会上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so...
zh: 所以……

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not just a change in the share of value that people transact over.
zh: 这不仅仅是人们在其中进行交易的价值份额的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a large growing pie.
zh: 这是一个巨大的、正在增长的蛋糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when that happens, it is actually possible to transition business models.
zh: 而当这种情况发生时，转型商业模式实际上是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, don't get me wrong, there are going to be winners and losers, right?
zh: 当然，别误会，会有赢家和输家，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like some pieces of content will become very valuable, some pieces of content will get more commoditized, and people are going to have to adapt to a new customer, to a new market dynamic, to a new kind of monetization engine.
zh: 比如有些内容会变得非常有价值，有些内容会更加商品化，人们将不得不去适应一个新客户、一种新的市场动态、一种新的变现引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the overall market size I think has the potential to increase unlike in music where it took a while for it to grow back.
zh: 但我认为整体市场规模有潜力增长，不像音乐行业那样花了一段时间才恢复。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think my understanding is now the industry has grown back up and exceeded its previous peaks in a material way.
zh: 我记得我了解到，现在这个行业已经恢复并且以显著的方式超过了它之前的峰值。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there was a moment where it was smaller.
zh: 但确实有一段时间它是缩小的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this case, that might be a very compressed period given how fast these things are growing.
zh: 在这个案例中，考虑到这些东西增长得如此之快，那可能是一个非常压缩的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone questions the sustainability of margin structures in this business.
zh: 所有人都在质疑这个行业利润率结构的可持续性。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about that as a business today?
zh: 你作为一家当今的企业是怎么看待这个问题的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, we're in the infrastructure business.
zh: 今天，我们处于基础设施行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have a real technical lead in terms of being able to do things at very high quality, very cheap.
zh: 我们有真正的技术领先优势，能够以非常高的质量、非常便宜地做成事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think of the tech we're building, right?
zh: 如果你想想我们正在构建的技术，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what are we doing?
zh: 比如，我们在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We like to give the highest quality answer.
zh: 我们希望给出最高质量的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make it fast, make it cheap.
zh: 做得快，做得便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Spend the least amount of computer doing it.
zh: 用最少的算力来完成它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we obsess about only these three things, right?
zh: 就是说，我们只执着于这三件事，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Quality, cost, latency.
zh: 质量、成本、延迟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turns out if you do that, relative to a stack built for humans over the last 20 years, you can do things at the same quality for 120th, 150th of the compute.
zh: 事实证明，如果你这样做，相对于过去 20 年为人类构建的技术栈，你可以用百分之一二十、百分之一五十的算力做到同样的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of margins come down to market structure on competition over time, rather than any other factor.
zh: 所以，随着时间推移，很多利润率其实归结为市场竞争结构，而不是任何其他因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in our industry, the market is large.
zh: 而在我们的行业，市场是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're too early to know what future competition and market structure looks like.
zh: 现在还太早，不知道未来的竞争和市场结构会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the margin change due to content owners is not something I worry about.
zh: 但内容所有者导致的利润率变化不是我所担心的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let me tell you why.
zh: 让我告诉你为什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: The entire premise of us paying content owners is driving incentive alignment.
zh: 我们向内容所有者付费的整个前提是在推动激励对齐。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we like to pay content owners the marginal contribution that they added to an agent doing work.
zh: 所以我们希望按照内容所有者为智能体完成工作所增加的边际贡献来向他们付费。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean?
zh: 这是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's assume that there's an agent trying to get something done, and you're going to spend a dollar on that agent to get this thing done.
zh: 假设有一个智能体试图完成某件事，而你要在这个智能体上花一美元来完成这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, if you've spent a dollar and 10 seconds, because we have a larger model available or ways of spending compute, you could have gotten a slightly better answer.
zh: 现在，如果你花了一美元和 10 秒钟，因为我们有一个更大的模型可用，或者说有花费算力的方法，你本可以得到一个稍微好一点的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you've spent 90 cents, you would have gotten a slightly worse answer.
zh: 如果你花了 90 美分，你会得到一个稍微差一点的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're running good agents, like they're on this Pareto curve.
zh: 如果你运行的是好的智能体，它们就在这条帕累托曲线上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now imagine I took out one content owner, their data from the web index, and I still spent a dollar.
zh: 现在想象一下，我从网络索引中去掉了一个内容所有者、他们的数据，而我仍然花了一美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: But let's say after taking them out,
zh: 但假设在把他们去掉之后，

speaker: Unknown
en: The quality of the result was the same as the 90 cent agent with their content.
zh: 结果的质量和有他们内容时的 90 美分智能体是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So why wouldn't we go and take this 10 cents of marginal contribution they had as a content owner and pay out a decent chunk of it to the person who brought that data?
zh: 那么为什么我们不把这个内容所有者所拥有的 10 美分的边际贡献，拿出相当大的一部分，付给带来那个数据的人呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how we do our math.
zh: 这就是我们做数学计算的方式。
